verdict.rationale: First-party docs state that once mise is activated in the shell (e.g. `mise activate bash`), entering a project puts its tool versions on PATH and loads its environment variables, then restores the environment when you leave. Env vars can come from `mise.toml`, .env files, secrets, and shell commands, and hierarchical configs are merged across parent directories. Community users corroborate it as a smooth asdf replacement with auto venv activation. Missing for 10: independent hands-on corroboration specifically of env-var loading/unloading on directory change, and detail on how the trust prompt and shims mode affect automatic activation.
